concept.name: Triangular moving average
concept.definition: A double-smoothed simple moving average — an SMA of an SMA — whose effective weights form a triangle that peaks at the middle of the window, giving mid-window data the most influence.
concept.intuition: Averaging an average: extra smooth at the cost of extra lag, with the middle of the window weighted most.
concept.mechanics: TMA(n) = SMA( SMA(P, m1), m2 ) with m1 = ceil((n+1)/2) and m2 = floor((n+1)/2); equivalently a single convolution with triangular weights 1, 2, ..., m, ..., 2, 1.
concept.failure_modes: Twice the smoothing means roughly twice the lag of its component SMA, so it is poor for timing and usable mainly as a slow trend reference.
concept.misconceptions: Despite the peaked weighting it is not centered in the signal sense — it uses past data only and still lags; a true centered moving average uses future data and cannot be computed in real time.
concept.example: A 5-period TMA = SMA(SMA(P, 3), 3); if the last three 3-period SMA values are 10, 11, 12, the TMA is 11.
